title: After 600 experiments, here's what I discovered about JEPA world models
short: 600 planning experiments on a JEPA world model (LeWM, Push-T)
author: Haddy Alchaer (independent)
more_note: Its interactive figures (the hero wall of solved runs, the memory graph with free and costed jumps, the rotated copies, the replay of the pusher-scored run) are worth opening there; this page redraws only the success rates, adds a toy of the jump cost and checks the numbers.
takeaway: On Push-T, in one author's single runs without retraining, LeWM (a 15M-parameter JEPA world model) planned as well as the simulator when both were given expert subgoals every 25 steps (78% against 77%, 250 tasks with the goal 75 steps away); subgoals found in a graph of its own embedded training demonstrations, with a cost on each jump between demonstrations, took such tasks from 22% to 85%. On the author's harder test the best planner reaches 56%. No code released.
verdict: Believe the direction: over 25 steps LeWM's predictor is not what limits it on Push-T, and short chained searches are what pay. Read the 85% as retrieval from demonstrations that also supply the test goals, the 60-point gain as a simulator planner under the author's block-only success test, and every number as one run on reused tasks, with no code to check.

code.n: The author's GitHub account (halcdev, his Hacker News name) has no repository for this work (checked 27 November 2026). The model and planner it starts from are public: lucas-maes/le-wm (MIT) on the galilai-group/stable-worldmodel library.

discussion.t: Hacker News: "After 600 experiments, here's what I discovered about JEPA world models"

responses.t: Why take test goals from the demonstrations at all?
responses.n: Even the harder test takes goals from demonstrations; the real task is any pose to any pose. Asks for independently sampled goals. No reply.

responses.t: Deleting the memories near the goal broke the planner
responses.n: The fall from 93% to 32% shows the method needs a stored state near the goal: "more or less testing on the training set".

responses.t: Planning through subgoals is known work, not a discovery
responses.n: Subgoal graphs over stored states are established (Search on the Replay Buffer); suggests a title naming LeWM and Push-T.

responses.t: Latent planning is model-predictive control; TD-MPC also learns the cost
responses.n: Latent planning is MPC with a learned model; TD-MPC also predicts the reward, so it ranks plans better.

responses.t: Would a classical planner solve this without a world model?
responses.n: Would probabilistic roadmaps, or a Gumbel MCTS repository that solves Push-T without training, do as well? Not compared on the post's tasks.

resources.t: LeWorldModel: Stable End-to-End Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture from Pixels
resources.by: Maes, Le Lidec, Scieur, LeCun, Balestriero, arXiv 2603.19312 (third-party)
resources.n: LeWM: a 15M-parameter JEPA trained from pixels with two loss terms (prediction and SIGReg); 96.0% on Push-T over 50 tasks with the goal 25 steps away, CEM planner, receding horizon of 25 steps. Its limitations section already names short horizons and dataset coverage.

config/eval/pusht.yaml: 50 episodes from pusht_expert_train, seed 42, goal 25 steps ahead, 50-step budget. The Push-T success test (stable-worldmodel, envs/pusht/env.py) needs the pusher and the block together within 20 pixels and the block within 20 degrees.

resources.t: LeJEPA: Provable and Scalable Self-Supervised Learning Without the Heuristics
resources.n: Where SIGReg, the regulariser that keeps LeWM's embeddings from collapsing, comes from.

resources.t: H-JEPA: End-to-End Learning of Hierarchical World Models for Visual Planning
resources.by: Zhang, Terver, Rabbat, LeCun, Balestriero, arXiv 2610.06805 (third-party)
resources.n: The learned hierarchy the post names as today's alternative: on Push-T two levels match or exceed LeWM, three levels fall back because Push-T's short episodes leave too few training clips. Its Push-T tasks use held-out expert frames 75 steps apart.

resources.t: Search on the Replay Buffer: Bridging Planning and Reinforcement Learning
resources.n: The memory-graph idea in 2019: a graph over stored states, edges weighted by a learned distance, shortest path as waypoints for a short-horizon controller.
An earlier graph of observations from a walkthrough, with learned shortcut edges and subgoals for a local policy.

resources.t: DINO-WM: World Models on Pre-trained Visual Features enable Zero-shot Planning
resources.n: The Push-T dataset, success test and planning setup LeWM inherits.

resources.t: What Drives Success in Physical Planning with Joint-Embedding Predictive World Models?
resources.n: A systematic study of the design choices in planning with JEPA world models, the paper-scale counterpart of the post's experiments (listed, not read for this page).
